events.title: Python 2.0 released
events.summary: Guido van Rossum released Python 2.0 on October 16, 2000 with list comprehensions, garbage collection, and Unicode support — defining Python for the next decade.
events.about: Python 2.0 added list comprehensions, `//` floor division, and a cycle-detecting GC — the dialect that powered YouTube's early stack, scientific computing, and countless scripts. Its long life eventually forced the painful Python 3 migration.

narrative.whyChosen: Python 2 defined the language for fifteen years before the Python 3 break.
narrative.whyImportant: List comprehensions and Unicode groundwork shaped how millions wrote Python.
narrative.problemSolved: Python 1.x lacked modern collection syntax and consistent text handling for a growing web.

events.title: Konqueror and KHTML shipped with KDE 2
events.summary: KDE 2.0 debuted Konqueror with the KHTML rendering engine on October 23, 2000 — a browser and file manager that later influenced WebKit and Safari.
events.about: KHTML became one of the most influential browser engines ever: Apple forked it into WebKit for Safari, which later powered Chrome via Blink. Konqueror itself was the default browser on Linux desktops and proved a small open-source team could ship a competitive engine.

narrative.whyChosen: KHTML is the ancestor of WebKit and Blink — engines that power most browsers today.
narrative.whyImportant: It broke the IE–Netscape duopoly at the engine level and gave Apple and Google a head start.
narrative.problemSolved: The Linux desktop needed an integrated browser and file manager that did not depend on proprietary code.
